The first was invalidated by my own bad ledger write; the second by four commits landing while it ran (04b6a938f, 6c0df7d7e, 960dd822b, 4b7d59349). The second was killed with TaskStop rather than protected — CLAUDE.md §6's 'an invalidated run is cheap and an idle wait is not' — but the deeper cost is the one AUT-PD-144 records: I did ~40 minutes of diagnosis on a collision a concurrent session was fixing at the same time, and only the rebase revealed it.
⚠ AND I HIT AUT-PD-144's OWN DEFECT WHILE FILING IT, TWICE. The first rebase took a concurrent session's rename of the duplicate id and discarded mine; the second, onto 469e8944d, found my ids AUT-PD-142/143 already taken by another session, so both rows were re-allocated to AUT-PD-143/144 with the count re-derived explicitly on the new base (275 entries, 0 duplicates) rather than assumed. ⛔ AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THAT RESOLUTION WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: `git checkout --theirs` DURING A REBASE MEANS THE COMMIT BEING APPLIED, NOT THE UPSTREAM, so it silently took my own ledger and dropped six upstream commits' worth of claims.
